questions.question: Define a hemisphere and explain how the four hemispheres are created. Name the hemispheres of Johannesburg, at 26°12′S 28°03′E, and of Tokyo, at about 35°41′N 139°41′E, giving reasons.
questions.expected_answer: A hemisphere is half of a sphere. The equator divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. The prime meridian at 0° and the 180° meridian together form a circle that divides the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres. Johannesburg is in the Southern Hemisphere because its latitude is south of the equator, and in the Eastern Hemisphere because its longitude is east of the prime meridian. Tokyo is in the Northern Hemisphere because its latitude is north, and in the Eastern Hemisphere because its longitude is east.

questions.question: Explain why Africa is the only continent in all four hemispheres, naming two countries crossed by the equator and one crossed by the prime meridian. Where is the official boundary between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans?
questions.expected_answer: Africa is crossed by both the equator and the prime meridian, so parts of it lie north, south, east and west of these lines. The equator crosses Gabon, the Republic of the Congo, the DRC, Uganda, Kenya and Somalia; the prime meridian crosses Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso and Ghana. The official boundary between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans is the meridian through Cape Agulhas, at about 20°E.

questions.question: Describe how land, water and people are distributed between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, and explain why the seasons are opposite in the two hemispheres in one sentence.
questions.expected_answer: The Northern Hemisphere has about two-thirds of the world's land and about nine out of ten of its people, though it is still about sixty percent water. The Southern Hemisphere is about four-fifths ocean, with Antarctica, Australia, most of South America and southern Africa as its main land. The seasons are opposite because the Earth's axis is tilted, so when one hemisphere is tilted towards the sun and has summer, the other is tilted away and has winter.
